strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear identification of key challenges (causalization and action conditioning)
Strong empirical results across diverse domains (robotics RT-1 and game simulation CS:GO) with consistent improvements over baselines
Clever mixed weight transfer scheme for temporal convolutions that preserves pre-trained information better than naive approaches
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including ablations, qualitative results, and downstream task validation (Real2Sim policy evaluation)
Systematic technical approach with clear algorithms and good reproducibility details provided
Demonstrates practical viability of adapting pre-trained video diffusion models to interactive world modeling
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: mixed weight transfer is incremental heuristic; relies heavily on existing techniques (Diffusion Forcing, causal masking, CFG); action dropout for guidance is straightforward
Severely limited experimental scope: only one base model tested (DynamiCrafter 1.1B/320×512); generalization to other video diffusion models, resolutions, or architectures unclear
Critical missing comparison: no evaluation against AVID [43], the most directly related recent work addressing the same problem
Insufficient validation of causalization claims: causal generation tested only indirectly through final video quality; no ablations removing history frames to verify predictions depend only on past
Arbitrary design choices without justification: action dropout p=0.2, guidance scale λ=2.5, rescale 0.7 appear unmotivated; mixed weight transfer initialization (mean) not compared to alternatives

Weak action conditioning evaluation: standard video metrics (FVD, SSIM) measure visual similarity not action responsiveness; no quantitative metrics for action-controlled generation quality; counterfactual reasoning only shown qualitatively
Limited downstream task evaluation: only one Real2Sim task (drawer closing) with modest sample size (N=80) and human verification; no other RL/planning tasks tested
Fairness concerns in baselines: non-autoregressive methods compared in autoregressive setting; different training setups make 7-day vs 100k-step comparison non-direct
Incomplete ablations: missing studies on action dropout probability, guidance hyperparameters, Diffusion Forcing contribution, alternative weight transfer schemes
Insufficient failure analysis: acknowledged failures (Figures 6, 10) not systematically characterized; 'regressing to familiar scenes' suggests mode collapse but prevalence/conditions unknown

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing the gap between non-interactive video diffusion models and interactive world models
Strong empirical results across domains (81.8% FVD improvement on CS:GO, significant gains on RT-1)
Technically sound approach combining diffusion forcing, causal architectures, and classifier-free guidance, with mixed weight transfer being a clever engineering contribution
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including multiple metrics, two diverse domains, ablation studies, and real2sim policy evaluation
Clear presentation with good intuitive figures (Figures 1-3) explaining the transformation pipeline
Thorough implementation details and hyperparameter documentation supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty—mostly combines existing techniques (diffusion forcing [8], classifier-free guidance [27], causal masking) with incremental new contributions (mixed weight transfer, action dropout)
Single base model (DynamiCrafter 1.1B) evaluated; acknowledged computational constraints prevent testing on larger models (Sora, Veo-2), limiting evidence of generalization
Weak baseline comparisons—all baselines adapted from same base model; no comparison with AVID [43] or other recent world modeling approaches
Insufficient generalization analysis—limited to specific datasets (RT-1 manipulation tasks, CS:GO Dust II map); no cross-domain evaluation

Incomplete design justification—action guidance hyperparameters (scale 2.5, rescale 0.7) appear manually tuned; mixed weight transfer uses mean aggregation without justification or comparison to alternatives
Limited downstream task evaluation—Real2Sim uses only one task with small sample (N=80), requires human verification (not scalable), no inference efficiency analysis
Lack of systematic analysis of failure modes beyond Figure 6; no discussion of stochasticity in generated sequences; missing investigation of when causal generation degrades performance
Missing thorough ablation studies on action dropout rate sensitivity and action guidance scale effectiveness; no systematic exploration of design choices
No runtime or efficiency comparison with baselines despite acknowledgment that training is 'time-consuming'
Evaluation heavily relies on pixel-level metrics (FVD, FID); limited assessment of semantic understanding, physics consistency, or long-horizon prediction quality

strengths: Novel problem formulation leveraging internet-scale video data through pre-trained diffusion models for world modeling
Principled approach to temporal convolution causalization using extrapolative weight transfer with theoretical error bounds
Comprehensive multi-domain experimental evaluation (RT-1, CS:GO, RECON) demonstrating significant improvements over baselines
Strong practical results with Real2Sim policy evaluation showing the method enables downstream decision-making tasks
High reproducibility with detailed algorithms, implementation details, and hyperparameter specifications
Clear presentation and well-motivated problem statement with effective use of figures and visualizations
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (causal masking, MLP action injection, classifier-free guidance); incremental contribution over prior work
Unfair baseline comparisons: most baselines are non-autoregressive and not designed for interactive generation, making the comparison with autoregressive Vid2World problematic
Theoretical gaps in extrapolative weight transfer: error bounds are loose (depend on uncharacterized smoothness constant L), linear approximation assumption not empirically validated

Incomplete experimental analysis: ablations use 30k steps vs 100k for main results limiting validity; missing sensitivity analyses for guidance scale and dropout rate; limited real2sim evaluation (50 trajectories, one task)
Limited model scale: 1.1B parameters is relatively lightweight; unclear how much improvement scaling provides and whether 'highly capable' characterization is justified
Insufficient failure mode analysis: acknowledges issues (fine-grained control, mode collapse) but provides limited investigation into when/why causalization or action conditioning fails
Limited evaluation scope: all domains are constrained closed-loop environments with short horizons (16 frames); no evaluation on open-ended scenarios or high-dimensional action spaces
Unjustified design choices: fixed guidance scale (2.5) across domains; p=2 for weight transfer with no sensitivity analysis; limited exploration of design space
